content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon when prices are trending downward or consolidating.
- Shows significant lag in reacting to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., spikes in history) — model peaks too early and then drops too fast.
- Tends to overcorrect downward trends — forecasts dip too aggressively, then rebound too soon.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring volatility persistence.
- Horizon-specific: 10-day forecasts are often too low; 20-day forecasts show more lag; 30-day forecasts are often too high early and too low late.
- Avoids recent volatility — ignores short-term momentum in history, especially after 5–7 days of strong movement.
